title_en: Owner's Committee of Chunjiang Garden, Wuxi City v. Shanghai Lujiazui Property Management Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over property management
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 72 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, an owner has rights and bears obligations with respect to the common areas of a building other than the exclusive parts. Income generated from common areas during the period of property management (including preliminary property management) by a property service enterprise shall, in the absence of a special agreement, belong to all owners and be mainly used to supplement the special maintenance fund of the residential community. Where a property service enterprise operates and manages the common areas, it may be entitled to a certain proportion of such income.

full_text_en:
Chunjiang Garden Owners' Committee of Wuxi City v. Shanghai Lujiazui Property Management Co., Ltd., et al.
— Dispute over Property Management

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to Article 72 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, owners have rights and assume obligations with respect to the common areas of a building other than the exclusive parts. Income generated from common areas during the period of property management (including preliminary property management) by a property service enterprise, in the absence of a special agreement, shall belong to all owners and shall be primarily used to supplement the special maintenance fund for the residential community. A property service enterprise that manages and operates common areas may be entitled to a certain proportion of such income.

Plaintiff: Chunjiang Garden Owners' Committee, Jiangsu Province, Wuxi City, domiciled at: Extension Section of Xueqian East Road, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province.

Representative: Chang Benjing, Director of the Owners' Committee.

Defendant: Shanghai Lujiazui Property Management Co., Ltd., Wuxi Branch, domiciled at: Chunjiang Garden Area B, Xishan Economic Development Zone, Xishan District, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province.

Representative: Yuan Guodong, Manager of the Branch.

Defendant: Shanghai Lujiazui Property Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Jin'an East Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Xu Erjin, Chairman of the Company.

The Plaintiff, Chunjiang Garden Owners' Committee of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as the "Owners' Committee"), filed a lawsuit with the Xishan District People's Court of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province, against the Defendant, Shanghai Lujiazui Property Management Co., Ltd., Wuxi Branch (hereinafter referred to as the "Wuxi Branch"), and the Defendant, Shanghai Lujiazui Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the "Property Company"), regarding a property management dispute.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On November 25, 2002, the Defendant Property Company entered into a preliminary property management entrustment contract with Wuxi Jujiang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Jujiang Company"), the developer of the Chunjiang Garden residential community. The contract stipulated that Jujiang Company entrusts the Property Company with the property management of Chunjiang Garden, with the management term commencing on November 25, 2002 and ending upon the establishment of the Owners' Committee of the Chunjiang Garden community. After the contract was established, the Property Company arranged for the Defendant Wuxi Branch to specifically implement the property management of Chunjiang Garden. On December 22, 2007, the Plaintiff Owners' Committee was legally established. On June 21, 2008, pursuant to the resolution on owner self-governance adopted by the Chunjiang Garden owners' general meeting, the Owners' Committee sent a letter to the Property Company, clearly stating that it would not renew the property management contract and requesting the Property Company to promptly complete the handover. On July 17, 2008, the Property Company sent personnel to formally handle the handover with the Owners' Committee and signed a handover list, which specified that the total amount of property management fees and other expenses to be handed over by the Property Company to the Owners' Committee was RMB 2,327,931.87, including the settlement period for income from the common areas of the community from January to June 2008. Upon reviewing the materials handed over by the Property Company, the Owners' Committee found that the Wuxi Branch had collected income from the common areas of the community totaling RMB 5,967,370.31 from 2004 to 2007, which had not been included in the handover. To protect the interests of all owners, the Owners' Committee filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting that the Property Company and the Wuxi Branch immediately return RMB 2,273,872.32 out of the RMB 2,327,931.87 confirmed in the handover list (the difference of RMB 54,059.55 being the portion agreed upon by both parties and recognized by the Owners' Committee as refundable to the Property Company after the agreement), plus 70% of the income from the common areas from 2004 to 2007, amounting to RMB 4,177,159.22, totaling RMB 6,451,031.54.

The Plaintiff Owners' Committee submitted the following evidence:

1. A copy of the filing certificate of the Plaintiff Owners' Committee and a copy of the filing receipt for the owners' committee within the property management area of Wuxi City, to prove the lawful establishment of the Owners' Committee.
2. A copy of the minutes of a meeting between the Plaintiff Owners' Committee and the Defendant Wuxi Branch on January 11, 2008, to prove that the Owners' Committee requested a handover of materials from the Wuxi Branch.
3. A copy of the minutes of a meeting between the Defendant Property Company and the Plaintiff Owners' Committee on June 23, 2008, to prove that the two parties discussed the handover matters after the Chunjiang Garden owners' self-governance.
4. A copy of a notice, to prove that the Plaintiff Owners' Committee notified the Defendant Property Company of the resolution of the Chunjiang Garden owners' general meeting to implement owner self-governance and requested the Property Company to hand over relevant materials and settle related labor wages and daily expenses.
5. A material handover agreement dated June 29, 2008, a document handover agreement dated June 29, 2008, and a Wuxi Chunjiang Garden external contract amendment agreement dated June 30, 2008, to prove that the Plaintiff Owners' Committee and the Defendant Property Company agreed to hand over related materials and items.
6. A Wuxi Chunjiang Garden withdrawal personnel relationship handling agreement signed on June 29, 2008, between the Plaintiff Owners' Committee and the Defendant Property Company, to prove that both parties arranged for the placement of relevant personnel.
7. A copy of "Regarding the Wuxi Chunjiang Garden Withdrawal Handover Agreement" dated July 17, 2008, to prove that the Defendant Property Company agreed to withdraw from the property management of Chunjiang Garden on June 23, 2008, and to hand over relevant materials.
8. A copy of "Property Company Chunjiang Garden Phase I and Phase II Settlement Payment Handover List" dated July 17, 2008. To prove that both parties reached an agreement on the property and funds that the Defendant Property Company should hand over to the Plaintiff Owners' Committee in 2008.
9. A letter dated July 21, 2008, from the Plaintiff Owners' Committee to the Defendant Property Company. To prove that the Owners' Committee requested the Property Company to confirm the series of agreements signed by its representative with the Owners' Committee between June 23, 2008, and July 17, 2008.
10. A reply letter dated July 29, 2008, from the Defendant Property Company to the Plaintiff Owners' Committee. To prove that the Property Company had no objection to the four agreements signed by both parties concerning personnel relationship handling, document handover, external contract signing, and material handover, and requested further negotiations on fee settlement. This supports the fact that the handover list of July 17, 2008, did not represent a complete resolution of all matters between the parties.
11. Income and expenditure statements for the years 2005 to 2007 prepared by the Defendant Wuxi Branch, and some daily fee collection and refund reports for 2004, to prove that the total income from the common areas from 2004 to 2007, amounting to RMB 5,967,370.31, should be handed over by the Defendant Property Company.

The Defendant Property Company and Wuxi Branch argued: On November 25, 2002, the Property Company negotiated and signed a preliminary property management contract with Jujiang Company, and the Wuxi Branch specifically implemented the property management of Chunjiang Garden. This is true. After the Plaintiff Owners' Committee was established, both parties successively handled the handover of materials, etc., and through settlement, signed a handover list on July 17, 2008, which clearly stated that as of June 30, 2008, the total amount the Property Company should settle to the Owners' Committee was RMB 2,327,931.87. This is a final settlement of the preliminary property management period and a package solution for all materials and property that should be handed over to the Owners' Committee. Article 10 of the handover list also clearly states: "Both parties agree that income and expenses that should be borne by each party during their respective management periods shall be borne by each party." According to this clause, it can be seen that all disputes between the parties have been fully resolved. Therefore, the Owners' Committee's current claims exceed the scope of the agreement, and the part of the claims exceeding the agreement should not be supported by the court. According to the agreement, the total amount that the Property Company and the Wuxi Branch should hand over to the Owners' Committee is RMB 2,327,931.87. After deducting the RMB 54,059.59 recognized by the Owners' Committee in its claim as payable to the Property Company, RMB 1,857,995.72 has already been paid. Therefore, RMB 415,876.6 remains to be handed over to the Owners' Committee. The Defendants agree to promptly hand over this amount.

In the alternative, even if the handover list did not include the income from the common areas from 2004 to 2007, the Plaintiff Owners' Committee's claims lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. The main reasons are: According to relevant laws and local regulations, the income from the common areas should first deduct costs to calculate the profit. This profit should first cover the Property Company's management costs, and the excess portion should also guarantee an 8% profit for the Property Company. Only then, if there is any remaining balance, can it be shared between the property management enterprise and the owners in a certain proportion. In this case, the Property Company and the Wuxi Branch's management of Chunjiang Garden was already marginally profitable, far from reaching an 8% profit margin. Therefore, after calculating the income from the management of the common areas of Chunjiang Garden from 2004 to 2007 using the above method, there is no distributable profit remaining. Furthermore, some owners in the community still owe property management fees of RMB 1,310,000 for the period up to June 30, 2008. Since the Owners' Committee represents all owners, the Defendants request to exercise a set-off right against this outstanding amount, deducting it from the funds the Property Company should hand over to the Owners' Committee.

The Defendant Property Company and Wuxi Branch submitted the following evidence:

1. A copy of the preliminary property management entrustment contract for Chunjiang Garden signed on November 25, 2002, between the Defendant Property Company and Jujiang Company, to prove the Property Company's qualification to implement preliminary property management for Chunjiang Garden.
2. A copy of an electronic bank transfer voucher from China Construction Bank, to prove that after signing the "Property Company Chunjiang Garden Phase I and Phase II Settlement Payment Handover List" on July 17, 2008, the Defendant Property Company fulfilled its payment obligation of RMB 557,995.72.
3. "Chunjiang Garden Management Office Operating Statements" from July 2006 to June 2008, to prove that the Defendant Property Company's property management operations at Chunjiang Garden were marginally profitable, with a profit of only RMB 63,539.46, and that the Plaintiff Owners' Committee's claims are unfounded.

Facts Found by the First Instance Court (Xishan District People's Court):

On November 25, 2002, the Defendant Property Company and the developer Jujiang Company negotiated and signed a preliminary property management contract for Chunjiang Garden. The contract stipulated that the Property Company would implement preliminary property management for the Chunjiang Garden residential community developed by Jujiang Company. The management scope covered Phases I, II, and III of Chunjiang Garden, covering an area of 323,000 square meters, with a building area of 600,000 square meters. It stipulated that during the management period, the Property Company would collect property management service fees from owners and property users based on the approved standards of the Price Bureau, calculated by building area. The property costs for shops, underground parking garages, and clubs within the property scope were not included in the property fees charged to owners and must be listed separately. The management term stipulated in the contract was from November 25, 2002 (the date of contract signing) until the establishment of the Owners' Committee. The contract also stipulated other related matters. After the contract was established, the Property Company assigned its subordinate branch, the Defendant Wuxi Branch, to specifically implement the preliminary property management of Chunjiang Garden.

On December 22, 2007, the Plaintiff Chunjiang Garden Owners' Committee was established. After its establishment, on January 2, 2008, it completed the registration and filing procedures with the Dongting Subdistrict Office of Xishan District, Wuxi City. On June 21, 2008, pursuant to the resolution on owner self-governance adopted by the owners' general meeting, the Owners' Committee sent a letter to the Defendant Property Company, clearly terminating the property management service contract, and requesting the Property Company to hand over relevant materials and property within 15 days of receiving the letter and complete the handover. Upon receiving the letter, the Property Company sent its Deputy General Manager, Zhu Jifeng, to negotiate with the Owners' Committee Director, Chang Benjing, on July 17, 2008, and reached a "handover list" with the nature of a handover agreement. The agreement confirmed that as of June 30, 2008, the total amount the Property Company should return to the Owners' Committee, including prepaid property management fees after July 1, 2008, various owner deposits held in custody, and income from the common areas of the community from January to June 2008, amounted to RMB 2,327,931.87. Of this, RMB 1,890,931.87 was to be paid in full before July 31, 2008, and the remaining RMB 437,000 was to be paid before April 30, 2009. Article 10 of the agreement also stipulated: "Both parties agree that income and expenses that should be borne by each party during their respective management periods shall be borne by each party." Attached to the agreement were a "Settlement Item List" and a "Payment Agreement," both confirmed by both parties. The "Settlement Item List" recorded that the parking fee income from the common areas of Chunjiang Garden collected in 2008 was RMB 629,035, and the parking fee for 2008 pre-collected in 2007 was RMB 160,180. 70% of this parking fee income was to be managed by the Owners' Committee, and the Property Company was to hand over this amount to the Owners' Committee.

During the trial of this case, on August 26, 2008, the Defendant Property Company voluntarily fulfilled a payment obligation of RMB 557,995.72. Subsequently, upon application by the Plaintiff Owners' Committee, the court ordered a preliminary execution of RMB 1,300,000 from the Property Company's bank deposits. In total, the Property Company actually paid RMB 1,857,995.72.

It was also found that according to the financial statements of the Defendant Wuxi Branch during the preliminary property management period, the income of the Wuxi Branch from managing the common areas of Chunjiang Garden included three items: site rental fees, parking management fees, and club income. Specifically: RMB 1,415,112.82 in 2005, RMB 1,808,004.50 in 2006, and RMB 2,144,933.00 in 2007. The expenditures for managing the common areas were: RMB 298,155.95 in 2005, RMB 497,204.12 in 2006, and RMB 430,131.07 in 2007. The difference between income and expenditure was RMB 4,142,559.18. The above expenditure items included property service expenses, parking management expenses, club expenses (including swimming pool expenses, maintenance expenses, and other expenses), and other business taxes (including business tax, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, price adjustment fund, grain risk fund, and flood control security fund). Both parties had no objection to the facts confirmed by the financial statements.

The above facts are confirmed by the evidence materials submitted by the Plaintiff Owners' Committee and the Defendants Property Company and Wuxi Branch, as well as the trial transcripts of this case, and are sufficient for determination.

The issues in dispute at first instance were:

1. Whether the handover agreement of July 17, 2008, included all settlement matters, particularly whether it included the income from the common areas for the years 2004 to 2007.
2. The definition and distribution of income from the common areas for 2004 to 2007.
3. Whether the Defendant Property Company could exercise a set-off right against the outstanding property management fees owed by some owners.

Opinion of the First Instance Court (Xishan District People's Court):

Regarding Disputed Issue 1: The content reflected in the handover agreement. The court held that: The handover agreement of July 17, 2008, represents the true intentions of both parties. The agreement provides detailed provisions on the funds the Defendant Property Company should return to the Plaintiff Owners' Committee for its management period in 2008, the owner deposits held in custody during the entire preliminary management period, and the delivery timeline. According to the agreement, the amount the Property Company should return to the Owners' Committee is RMB 2,327,931.87. However, it is noteworthy that the agreement does not specifically record the income from the Property Company's and the Defendant Wuxi Branch's management of the common areas of the community from 2004 to 2007. According to the Wuxi Branch's financial statements, this portion of income is substantial. During the trial of this case, the Property Company and the Wuxi Branch interpreted Article 10 of the agreement, "Both parties agree that income and expenses that should be borne by each party during their respective management periods shall be borne by each party," to mean that by signing this clause, both parties reached a package solution regarding the handover content, and there are no other disputes. Even if there are remaining disputes, each party should bear them and not claim against the other. The Owners' Committee, however, argued that this clause only indicates that there are no further disputes regarding the items listed in the handover list and does not imply that it has waived its right to claim distribution of the income from the common areas. The court held that the handover agreement between the parties explicitly hands over the income from the common areas for January to June 2008. Furthermore, the content of Article 10 cannot be interpreted as the Owners' Committee expressing an intention to waive its rights to the income from the common areas of Chunjiang Garden before 2008. Therefore, the agreement should be considered an incomplete handover agreement, as it does not include the income from the common areas for 2004 to 2007. Moreover, according to the Wuxi Branch's statements, the income from the common areas for 2004 to 2007 was substantial. The Owners' Committee, as an organization exercising rights on behalf of all owners, derives its authority from the mandate of the owners' general meeting. Without authorization from all owners, it cannot waive major rights of the owners based on its own will. Even if it expressed such an intention to waive, that act would be a void civil act. Accordingly, the court held that the income from the common areas for 2004 to 2007 was not reflected in the aforementioned handover agreement and should be distributed between the property management enterprise and all owners in accordance with the law.

Regarding Disputed Issue 2: The definition and distribution of income from the common areas for 2004 to 2007. The court held that: In this case, the so-called property management income from the common areas should be the difference between income and cost expenditures of the common areas. Both parties reached an agreement during the trial that the income and expenditures of the common areas of Chunjiang Garden from 2004 to 2007 should be based on the statements of the Defendant Wuxi Branch. This civil act of both parties does not violate prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations, and the court confirms it. Upon reviewing the relevant statements, the total income from the common areas of the community for 2005 to 2007 was RMB 5,368,050.32, the total expenditure during that period was RMB 1,225,491.14, resulting in a total profit of RMB 4,142,559.18. Regarding the Plaintiff Owners' Committee's claim for income in 2004, the statements it provided do not allow for a determination of this income. The parties were also unable to reach a consensus on the income from the common areas for that year. The Owners' Committee, as the party asserting the right, bears the burden of proof and must bear the adverse consequences of failing to provide sufficient evidence. Therefore, due to insufficient evidence, the court does not support the Owners' Committee's claim for distribution of income for 2004.

Regarding the Distribution of Income. The court held that the income in dispute in this case arose, on the one hand, from the management activities of the defendant Property Management Company and Wuxi Branch, and on the other hand, it should be noted that the property managed by the property management enterprise is jointly owned by all owners. Co-owners have the right to income from the co-owned property, which is a statutory right. The distribution of this portion of income may be agreed upon by all owners and the property management enterprise through contract; in the absence of agreement, it shall be distributed according to law. In this case, there is no contractual basis for the distribution of this portion of income between the parties, so distribution must be made in accordance with legal provisions. Since the laws of our country have no specific provisions on this matter, the court held that the management income from the common parts of the property should be distributed fairly and reasonably, without violating legal principles. Property management has its particularities; during the implementation of property management, the property management enterprise serves the owners of the community, and the owners do not provide compensation for the management of the common parts. If the property management enterprise incurs management costs but cannot obtain economic returns, it would be unfair to the property management enterprise. At the same time, since the common parts of the community are the common property of all owners in the community, the owners are the owners of such property. If the owners' rights are excluded from the distribution of income, this would obviously be contrary to legal principles. Accordingly, where there is income from the management of the common parts of the community, such income should primarily belong to all owners. At the same time, the property management enterprise, having incurred management costs, should also be entitled to a reasonable return. In summary, based on the principle of fairness and with reference to the spirit of Article 33 of the *Jiangsu Province Property Management Regulations*, which provides that "the income from approved commercial facilities, after deducting the agency fees of the property management enterprise, shall use 30% of the income to subsidize the public property management service fee, and 70% of the income shall be allocated to the maintenance fund, unless otherwise agreed in the contract." Also, considering the distribution plan for the income from common parts for the first half of 2008, which was voluntarily agreed upon by the plaintiff and the defendant (i.e., owners receive 70%, property management enterprise receives 30%), the court held that it is reasonable to determine the proportion of distribution for the income from common parts in this case as 70% for the plaintiff Owners' Committee and 30% for the Property Management Company. Accordingly, the Owners' Committee, representing all owners of Chunjiang Garden, is entitled to RMB 2,899,791.43 of the total income of RMB 4,142,559.18. It is noteworthy that the Owners' Committee does not have the right to dispose of this portion of funds on its own. According to relevant laws and regulations, this amount shall be used as the maintenance fund for the community. As the executing body, the Owners' Committee shall use such funds in accordance with the will of the owners and the provisions of the law. Regarding the Property Management Company's opinion that the above income should first be used to cover the property management enterprise's management expenses, and the surplus should also satisfy an 8% profit for the property management enterprise, with the balance to be distributed, the court did not adopt this opinion due to lack of legal basis and mutual agreement between the parties.

Regarding Disputed Issue 3: Whether the defendant Property Management Company can exercise the right of set-off against the outstanding property management fees of some owners. The Property Management Company claimed that some owners had outstanding property management fees of RMB 1,310,000 for the period before June 30, 2008, but it did not submit sufficient evidence to prove this. More importantly, Article 99 of the *Contract Law of the People's Republic of China* provides: "If the parties mutually owe matured liabilities, and the subject matter of the liabilities is of the same kind and quality, either party may set off its own liability against the liability of the other party, except where set-off is not allowed according to legal provisions or the nature of the contract." According to this provision, for debt set-off to occur, the parties must owe liabilities to and hold claims against each other. In this case, the parties to the litigation are the plaintiff Owners' Committee and the Property Management Company and its Wuxi Branch, whereas the owners who owe property management fees are individual entities. The Owners' Committee filed the lawsuit on behalf of all owners in the community. Although this includes the owners who owe fees, there is a fundamental difference between the two. Therefore, the subjects of the claims and debts are different, which does not meet the requirements for statutory set-off. Accordingly, the Property Management Company's claim to exercise the right of set-off is not supported.

In summary, the defendant Property Management Company shall return to the plaintiff Owners' Committee the funds confirmed in the handover list (minus RMB 54,059.55) and 70% of the income from the common parts of the community from 2005 to 2007, i.e., the amount of RMB 2,273,872.32 confirmed by both parties, plus the income from the common parts to be returned to the owners amounting to RMB 2,899,791.43, totaling RMB 5,173,663.75. Given that the Property Management Company has already performed RMB 1,857,995.72, it still owes the Owners' Committee RMB 3,315,668.03. Since the defendant Wuxi Branch is a subordinate branch of the Property Management Company without independent legal personality, but was lawfully established with certain organizational structure and property, and also specifically implemented the property management activities, it shall bear the liability for the above return jointly with the Property Management Company. Accordingly, the Xishan District People's Court of Wuxi City, in accordance with Articles 70, 73, Paragraph 3 of Article 74, and Article 79 of the *Property Law of the People's Republic of China*, Paragraph 2 of Article 54 and Article 55 of the *Regulations on Property Management* of the State Council, and with reference to Article 33 of the *Jiangsu Province Property Management Regulations*, rendered the following judgment on June 12, 2009:

1. The defendant Property Management Company and Wuxi Branch shall jointly return RMB 3,315,668.03 to the plaintiff Owners' Committee within three days after this judgment takes effect.

2. The remaining claims of the plaintiff Owners' Committee are dismissed.

After the judgment was pronounced at the first instance, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory time limit, and the judgment has become legally effective.
